subject.name_or_desc: A citizen of London (the querent), asking concerning his absent brother

context.question: (1) If living or dead; if dead, whether killed by soldiers? (2) When should he hear of him, and where was he? (3) When would he come home?
context.asked_at: November 1645, about 4 p.m. London time: the question was asked the same day the trine of Venus and Saturn perfected — Lilly finds in the ephemeris the true time of the aspect at five of the clock that afternoon, 'but with reduction to our London Meridian little after four'.
context.setting: In November 1645 the brother was gone into the west of England, and no news had been heard of him for many weeks, the kingdom at that time being full of soldiers.

attachments.key_positions: Venus, lady of the third house (significatrix of the absent brother), in no manner of way afflicted either by Mercury, lord of the eighth in the figure, or by Mars; Venus applying to a trine of Saturn, lord of the Ascendant; Venus leaving a northern sign and entering into a south sign, wanting one degree of leaving the sign
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; one scheme serves the three queries (printed as Figs. 7–8 in the 1852 edition).

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, third-house chapter: judgment of an absent brother (Figs. 7–8 in the 1852 Zadkiel edition)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
